description.narrative: The objective of the Multisectoral Early Childhood Development Project for Marshall Islands is to improve coverage of multisectoral early childhood development services. There are four components to the project, the first component being improve coverage of essential RMNCH-N services. This component aims to improve the availability and coverage of an evidence-based package of essential RMNCH-N and stimulation services for the first 1,000 days. The component has two sub-components, one aimed at strengthening stewardship and management of health administration and the other at directly strengthening service delivery. The second component is the improve coverage of stimulation and early learning activities. Component two aims to improve children's cognitive and socio-emotional development and facilitate children's readiness for on-time transition to primary school through expanding access to stimulation and early learning services. This component includes two subcomponents: strengthening MOEST management and stewardship of ECD services; and enhancing delivery of stimulation and early learning activities. The third component is the social assistance for early years families. This component aims to introduce a conditional cash transfer (CCT) pilot to modify care practices and behaviors and promote uptake of ECD services. This component includes two subcomponents: strengthening Government of RMI's capacity to establish and deliver social assistance program for ECD, and provision of cash transfers to early years families in selected areas. Finally, the fourth component is the strengthening the multisectoral ECD system and project management. This component includes two subcomponents: national multisectoral ECD strategy and governance, and ECD awareness and SBCC campaign.
To improve coverage of multisectoral early childhood development services

condition.narrative: Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall maintain the Early Childhood Development CabinetCommittee until the closing date, and shall provide high level strategic leadership and guidance for the Project through the EarlyChildhood Development Cabinet Committee in accordance with the provisions of the Financing Agreement and the Project OperationsManual.
Section I.A.3 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall maintain until the closing date the Program SteeringCommittee.

Section I.A.5 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:To this end, the Recipient shall, by no later than three months after theEffective Date, establish and thereafter maintain until the closing date, the Early Childhood Development Working Group.

Section I.A.6 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall establish, by no later than three months after theEffective Date, and thereafter maintain until the closing date, the Project Implementation Unit within the Office of the ChiefSecretary.
Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall prepare and adopt, by no later than three (3) monthsafter the Effective Date, the Project Operations Manual.
Section I.B.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordancewith the provisions of the Project Operations Manual.

Section I.D of Schedule 2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:To facilitate the carrying out of Part 3 of the Project, theRecipient shall sign a Memorandum of Understanding, in form and substance acceptable to the Association, between the Ministry ofCulture and Internal Affairs, the Ministry of Education, Sports and Training, the Ministry of Health and Human Services, the MajuroAtoll Local Government, and Marshall Islands Social Security Administration detailing the division of responsibilities andcooperative arrangements for implementing Part 3 of the Project.

Section I.E of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out with due regard toappropriate health, safety, social, and environmental practices and standards, and in accordance with the Safeguards Instruments.

Section I.F of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association not laterthan:(a) four (4) months after the Effective Date (or such later date as the Association may agree); and (b) August 31 of eachyear for every subsequent year during the implementation of the Project (or such later date as the Association may agree);for theAssociation's no-objection, an Annual Work Plan and Budget.

Section II.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not laterthan forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar semester, covering the calendar semester.

Section II.2. of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The Recipient shall, not later than December, 2022 (or such other date asthe Association may agree in writing), prepare and furnish to the Association a mid-term report.

title.narrative: Number of RMNCH-N providers undergoing regular performance monitoring

comment.narrative: <p>No data are available. Related project activities will be initiated under ECD-II.</p>

title.narrative: Share of children aged 0-2 years who receive well-child visits as per established government guidelines*

comment.narrative: <p>The design of the CCT pilot program includes soft conditionalities in the initial phase of implementation. Compliance with conditionalities was not imposed during the life of the project and is being introduced under ECD-II (i.e. 12 months after the first tranche).</p>

title.narrative: Implementation of the GRM and resolution of grievances within agreed timeframes (Percentage)

comment.narrative: <p>One grievance (n=1) was resolved within the agreed timeframe and during the life of the project, 100 percent of grievances were resolved within the agreed timeframe. All grievances have been acknowledged and responded to within the agreed timeframe.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: <p>One hundred and nineteen (119) beneficiaries received the first distribution of the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) pilot program on 28 October 2022. The first tranche reached 119 beneficiaries through Bank of the Marshall Islands (BOMI) accounts. The first tranche was rationed toward the more vulnerable early years families utilizing poverty means testing scores of household characteristics.  This demonstrates progress against the intermediate indicator.</p>

title.narrative: Number of health workers trained in maternal, infant, and young child nutrition promotion (or, trained to deliver a package of essential RMNCH-N services)

comment.narrative:
<p>Intermediate target 1 achieved. Fifteen (15) Health Assistants were trained in 2021. The training was part of the College of the Marshall Islands (CMI) Health Assistant (HA) vocational certificate program. The program included training related to Maternal Child Health (MCH) and maternal, infant, and young child nutrition promotion.</p>
<p>Data source: College of the Marshall Islands (CMI) vocational certificate program for Health Assistants, 2021</p>

title.narrative: Number of teaching aides, parent educators, coaches and MOEST/PSS staff receiving training under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator end target achieved and exceeded. 453<strong> </strong>teaching aides, parent educators, coaches, and MOEST/PSS staff received training under the project (3+12+129+215+93+1).  Three (3) preschool Teaching Assistants participated in a series of trainings including preservice orientation training and in-service summer training. Twelve (12) parent educators, including two (2) parent educators based in Ebeye participated in full training and practicum delivered by the Pacific Regional Education Laboratory (PREL). One hundred and twenty-nine (129) Early Childhood Educators (ECE) participated in the Social-Emotional Learning for the Preschool Classroom training in the summer of 2021. The training piloted new teacher training materials (modules and handbook) developed for the Asia-Pacific region by UNESCO and the Asia-Pacific Regional Network for Early Childhood (ARNEC). Two-hundred and fifteen (215) educators from public and private schools participated in the special Teacher Self-Care module provided by the RMI Mental Health Coalition in the summer of 2021. This module was important as a precursor for the SEL training. Ninety-three (93) Early Childhood Educators earned certificates in the Disability Inclusive Education training in the summer of 2022. One (1) Nationa ECD Coordinator has been pursuing her master’s in education, she currently has a 4.0 GPA and will graduate in the summer of 2023</p>

title.narrative: People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services

comment.narrative:
<p>Intermediate target 2 achieved. Eight thousand, seventy-five (8,075) people received essential health, nutrition, and population services at completion. Patient encounters related to family planning, the Maternal Child Health clinic, immunizations for children aged 0 to 5 years, and ANC or post-partum patients.</p>

<p>Data source: Health Informatics 2022, MOHHS</p>

title.narrative: Number of children aged 3-4 attending preschool

comment.narrative:
<p>At appraisal, only private preschool services were available. In the Academic Year 2018 to 2019, there were one hundred sixty-nine (169) children aged 3 and 4 years enrolled in private preschool services, largely in urban areas; this is considered the revised baseline for this indicator (from 238 to 169). The project introduced public preschool services to a wider array of early years families, and by Academic Year 2022 to 2023, there were two-hundred forty-seven (247) children aged 3 and 4 years old enrolled in public (122 children) or private (125 children) preschool services. This equates to an increase of 157 children aged 3 and years old attending preschool relative to the baseline (an increase of almost 50 percent). Increasing the number of children with regular participation in play-based learning at their local preschool is likely to have made a positive impact on the number of Marshallese children aged 3 to 5 years that are developmentally on track.</p>
<p>Note on sub-indicator: <strong>BASELINE TBC</strog></p>

comment.narrative:

<p>Data source: MIHS, Ebeye, & Neighboring Island report, MOHHS. </p>

title.narrative: Share of children aged 3 and 4 years attending pre-school

comment.narrative: <p>Intermediate target 2 achieved. At appraisal, only private preschool services were available. In the Academic Year 2018 to 2019, there were one hundred sixty-nine (169) children aged 3 and 4 years enrolled in private preschool services, largely in urban areas. The project introduced public preschool services to a wider array of early years families, and by Academic Year 2022 to 2023,here were two-hundred forty-seven (247) children aged 3 and 4 years old enrolled in public (122 children) or private (125 children) preschool services. This equates to 10.5 percent of the total children aged 3 and 4 years old attending preschool.  </p>

title.narrative: Number of families with children aged 0-4 years receiving home visits from parent educators

comment.narrative:
<p>Intermediate target 2 achieved. Women United Together Marshall Islands (WUTMI) was providing the Ajri In Ibwinini home visit program to eighty-five (85) client families at project approval (baseline). By 31 December 2022, with the project-sponsored expansion of the Ajri In Ibwinini home visit program, WUTMI had expanded the program to one hundred eighty-five (185) client families. WUTMI has also extended the number of client families and the geographic spread of services on Majuro Atoll. They have also taken steps to increase the quality of their home visit program by re-instating their status as an affiliate provider of the Parents as Teachers program. The home visit program targets vulnerable families with young children, prenatally and up to age 4.</p>
<p>Data source: WUTMI Ajri In Ibwinini Quarterly Report, July to September 2022</p>
